seafile.description: Self-hosted file sync and share with real file-level versioning and client-side encryption options. Runs 3 containers (mariadb, memcached, seafile), with seafile listening on port 80 and keeps its data in named volumes.

searxng.description: A privacy-respecting metasearch engine that aggregates results from dozens of search services. Runs 2 containers (redis, searxng), with searxng listening on port 8080; data is kept in named volumes.

seaweedfs.description: A distributed file and object store with an S3 gateway, built for billions of small files. Runs as a single container from the seaweedfs image, listening on port 9333 and keeps its data in named volumes.

sftpgo.description: An SFTP, FTP/S, and WebDAV server with a web admin UI and per-user storage backends. Runs as a single container from the sftpgo image, listening on port 8080 and keeps its data in named volumes.

snipe-it.description: IT asset management for tracking hardware, licenses, and accessories, and who currently has what. Runs 2 containers (db, snipeit), with snipeit listening on port 80 and keeps its data in named volumes.

sonarr.description: Watches your favorite indexers for new TV episodes and automatically grabs, sorts, and renames them. Runs as a single container from the sonarr image, listening on port 8989; data is kept in named volumes.

speedtest-tracker.description: Runs Ookla speed tests on a schedule and charts your connection's throughput, latency, and jitter over time. Runs as a single container from the speedtest-tracker image, listening on port 80; data is kept in named volumes.

stalwart.description: An all-in-one SMTP, IMAP, JMAP, and WebDAV mail server in a single lightweight container. Runs as a single container from the stalwart image, listening on port 8080; data is kept in named volumes.

static-site-api-starter.description: A static frontend and a separate API service deployed together, the split most SPAs actually run. Runs 2 containers (api, static), with api listening on port 4000.

statusnook.description: Deploy a status page and start monitoring endpoints in minutes. Runs as a single container from the statusnook image, listening on port 8000; data is kept in named volumes.

supertokens.description: A self-hosted authentication backend with session management, social login, and passwordless, backed by Postgres. Runs 2 containers (postgres, supertokens), with supertokens listening on port 3567 and keeps its data in named volumes.

sure.description: A privacy-first personal finance app for tracking net worth, budgets, and investments across every account. Runs 4 containers (postgresql, valkey, web, worker), with web listening on port 3000 and keeps its data in named volumes.

syncthing.description: Continuous, peer-to-peer file synchronization between your own devices, no cloud in between. Runs as a single container from the syncthing image, listening on port 8384 and keeps its data in named volumes.

tautulli.description: Monitors your Plex server and shows who watched what, with history, stats, and notifications. Runs as a single container from the tautulli image, listening on port 8181; data is kept in named volumes.

tdarr.description: Automated media transcoding, health checks, and library-wide format standardization. Runs as a single container from the tdarr image, listening on port 8265; data is kept in named volumes.

technitium-dns.description: A full-featured authoritative and recursive DNS server with DNS-over-HTTPS/TLS and a web console. Runs as a single container from the dns-server image, listening on port 5380 and keeps its data in named volumes.

temporal.description: Durable workflow execution: write long-running business logic as code and let Temporal survive failures. Runs 3 containers (db, temporal, temporal-ui), with temporal listening on port 7233 and keeps its data in named volumes.

traccar.description: An open-source GPS tracking platform supporting over 170 device protocols. Runs 2 containers (traccar, traccar-db), with traccar listening on port 8082 and keeps its data in named volumes.

transmission.description: A fast, lightweight BitTorrent client with a simple web interface. Runs as a single container from the transmission image, listening on port 9091; data is kept in named volumes.

umami.description: Simple, privacy-focused website analytics without tracking cookies or ad-tech. Runs 2 containers (db, umami), with umami listening on port 3000 and keeps its data in named volumes.

uptime-kuma-mariadb.description: Uptime Kuma with a MariaDB sidecar provisioned, for the setups that opt out of its default SQLite file. Runs 2 containers (mariadb, uptime-kuma), with uptime-kuma listening on port 3001; data is kept in named volumes.

valkey.description: A Redis-compatible in-memory key-value store under the Linux Foundation, with password auth and append-only persistence. Runs as a single container from the valkey image, listening on port 6379; data is kept in named volumes.

vault.description: HashiCorp Vault for secrets storage, encryption as a service, and dynamic credentials, in file-storage mode. Runs as a single container from the vault image, listening on port 8200 and keeps its data in named volumes.

vaultwarden.description: A lightweight, self-hosted password manager server compatible with the Bitwarden clients. Runs as a single container from the server image, listening on port 80 and keeps its data in named volumes.

victoriametrics.description: A fast, resource-frugal time-series database that speaks the Prometheus query and remote-write APIs. Has no authentication, so point Prometheus-style senders at victoriametrics:8428 from other services in this project, or attach a domain only behind Basic Auth. Not published on the host. Runs as a single container from the victoria-metrics image, listening on port 8428; data is kept in named volumes.

vvveb.description: A CMS for building websites, blogs, and ecommerce stores. Runs as a single container from the vvvebcms image, listening on port 80; data is kept in named volumes.

wallos.description: A personal subscription tracker that shows what you pay each month, with reminders and multi-currency support. Runs as a single container from the wallos image, listening on port 80 and keeps its data in named volumes.

weaviate.description: An open-source vector database with hybrid search, built-in modules, and a GraphQL and REST API. Runs as a single container from the weaviate image, listening on port 8080; data is kept in named volumes.

whoogle.description: A privacy-focused front end for Google search results, with no tracking, ads, or JavaScript required. Runs as a single container from the whoogle-search image, listening on port 5000 and keeps its data in named volumes.

windmill.description: Turn scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, and SQL into webhooks, workflows, and internal UIs. Runs 2 containers (db, windmill), with windmill listening on port 8000 and keeps its data in named volumes.

wordpress.description: The world's most widely used content management system, self-hosted with its own database. Runs 2 containers (db, wordpress), with wordpress listening on port 80; data is kept in named volumes.

worker-redis-queue-starter.description: A worker process pulling jobs off a Redis-backed queue, the base shape for async job processing. Runs 2 containers (queue, worker) and keeps its data in named volumes.

yamtrack.description: A self-hosted media tracker for movies, TV, anime, manga, games, and books. Runs 2 containers (redis, yamtrack), with yamtrack listening on port 8000; data is kept in named volumes.

zabbix.description: Enterprise-grade network, server, and application monitoring with alerting and trend graphs. Runs 3 containers (db, zabbix-server, zabbix-web), with zabbix-web listening on port 8080; data is kept in named volumes.

zipline.description: A self-hosted file and screenshot host with a share-first upload flow and its own URL shortener. Runs 2 containers (db, zipline), with zipline listening on port 3000 and keeps its data in named volumes.
